mainTopic: Unborn babies at the sea, איוב serving God from love, love versus fear, and the start of the chapter מי שקינא on witnesses to a סוטה's seclusion and defilement.
overview: This amud finishes a teaching about שירת הים: even babies in the womb sang, and רבי תנחום explains that they could see because the belly became like clear glass. Then the גמרא turns to the משנה's teaching that איוב served God out of love. It asks why the spelling of the word לא doesn't settle the matter, and shows from a פסוק in ישעיהו that ל־א can mean either 'not' or 'to Him'. So רבי מאיר proves it another way: both איוב and אברהם are called 'God-fearing', and אברהם's fear came from love. The גמרא explains that serving from love is greater: its merit lasts two thousand generations instead of one thousand, based on two פסוקים. A story with רבא and two students shows that serving from fear and serving from love are both complete righteousness. The chapter כשם שהמים ends, and the new chapter's משנה begins. It discusses when a warned wife who secluded herself must be divorced, and whose testimony about her defilement is believed. A פסוק teaches that even one witness is enough, and a new קל וחומר about the seclusion testimony begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A verse shows even unborn babies praised God
steps.stepSummary: The previous teaching taught that even babies in the womb sang at the sea. This step brings a פסוק from תהלים as its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In assemblies, bless God, the Lord, you who are from the source of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a teaching about the song at the sea. It brings a פסוק showing that even those still in the 'source', meaning the mother's womb, blessed God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'from the source of Israel' are read as the unborn babies inside their mothers. So when everyone gathered and sang at the sea, even the babies in the womb joined in. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Gatherings, assemblies
Source; here read as the mother's womb
Bless! (a command to praise God)

phrases.english: "In assemblies, bless God,
phrases.notes: תהלים 68:27

phrases.english: the Lord, you who are from the source of Israel."
phrases.notes: The 'source' here is read as the mother's womb, so even unborn babies are included.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַקְהֵלוֹת בָּרְכוּ אֱלֹהִים ה׳ מִמְּקוֹר יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a teaching from the previous daf about who sang at the sea.
steps.raayaObject: That even babies in the womb sang שירת הים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 68:27, 'from the source of Israel', read as from the womb.

steps.title: But unborn babies cannot see
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that unborn babies sang 'this is my God', since they could not see anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they could not see!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the last step. If the babies were still inside their mothers, how could they see God's miracles and point to Him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The song at the sea includes the words 'זה אלי ואנוהו', 'this is my God', which sounds like pointing at something you see. A baby in the womb cannot see. So how could they honestly say it?

keyTerms.meaning: But surely (opens a challenge)
They saw

phrases.english: But they could not see!
phrases.notes: He means the unborn babies. How could they sing about something they never saw?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לָא חֲזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the teaching in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that babies in the womb sang at the sea.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Singing 'this is my God' needs seeing, and babies in the womb cannot see.

steps.title: The belly became like clear glass
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום answers that the mother's belly became like shining glass, so the babies could see through it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום said: The belly became for them like a shining glass, and they saw.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי תנחום answers the question. God made a miracle: the mother's belly became see-through, like clear glass, so the babies really saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the babies could not see. רבי תנחום says that normally that is true, but here there was a miracle. So the babies did see, and their song was real.

keyTerms.meaning: Belly, stomach
A shining, clear glass or mirror

steps.whatToRemember: At the sea, everyone saw God's miracles clearly, even the unborn, because a miracle let them see through the belly.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum said:
The belly became for them
like a shining glass, and they saw.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Babies in the womb could not see, so they could not have sung 'this is my God'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The belly became see-through, so they saw and truly sang.

steps.title: The משנה: איוב served God out of love
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, where רבי יהושע בן הורקנוס taught that איוב served God only out of love.
steps.simpleTranslation: On that day רבי יהושע בן הורקנוס taught that איוב served God only out of love, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says איוב served God out of love, based on the פסוק 'הן יקטלני לו איחל', 'Though He slay me, I will hope lo'. The word לו or לא can mean 'to Him' or 'not'. That doubt is what the גמרא will now ask about.

keyTerms.meaning: On that same day
Taught, explained a פסוק
Job

phrases.english: On that same day taught
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hyrcanus
that Job served only, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: only out of love. It's from איוב 13:15, where the key word could mean 'to Him' or 'not'.

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן הוּרְקָנוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איוב served God out of love.

steps.title: Why not just check the spelling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why there is any doubt. Just look at how the word is spelled: with ל־א it means 'not', and with ל־ו it means 'to Him'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us just look at this word לא. If it is written with ל־א, it means 'not'. If it is written with ל־ו, it means 'to Him'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's doubt about the word. It says the answer should be simple: check the spelling in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the word as unclear. But in Hebrew, 'not' is spelled לא and 'to Him' is spelled לו. So the spelling seems to decide it, and there should be no question.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us look and see
It is written
'Not' (spelled ל־א) or 'to Him' (spelled ל־ו); both sound the same

steps.confusionAlert: לא and לו sound exactly the same when read aloud. That is why there is a question at all; only the spelling is different.

phrases.english: Let us just look at this word "lo":
if it is written with lamed-alef,
it means "not";
if it is written with lamed-vav,
it means "to Him"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיחְזֵי הַאי לֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the doubt in the משנה from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that the meaning of the word is in doubt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The spelling in the פסוק should clearly decide whether it means 'not' or 'to Him'.

steps.title: Spelling with ל־א does not always mean 'not'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: ל־א does not always mean 'not'. In ישעיהו, 'In all their affliction He was lo afflicted' is spelled ל־א, but it surely does not mean God was not afflicted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And wherever it is written with ל־א, does it mean 'not'? If so, then 'בכל צרתם לא צר', 'In all their affliction He was afflicted', which is written with ל־א, would you say there too that it means 'not'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the idea that spelling settles the question. It brings a פסוק spelled ל־א that clearly means 'to Him'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 assumed ל־א always means 'not'. The פסוק in ישעיהו is spelled ל־א, yet it means God shares in Israel's pain. So spelling alone cannot prove the meaning, and the doubt in the משנה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then (shows a bad result of an idea)
Trouble, affliction
Would you say the same here too?

steps.whatToRemember: The spelling of לא does not settle its meaning, so it is still unclear whether איוב said 'not' or 'to Him'.

phrases.english: And wherever it is written with lamed-alef,
does it mean "not"?
If so, then
"In all their affliction He was lo afflicted",
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 63:9

phrases.english: which is written with lamed-alef,
would you say there too that it means "not"?
phrases.notes: Of course not. That פסוק means God feels Israel's pain, so here ל־א means 'to Him'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דִּכְתִיב בְּלָמֶד אָלֶף לֹא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 by rejecting its assumption.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The rule that spelling with ל־א always means 'not'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ישעיהו 63:9 is spelled ל־א but means 'to Him', so spelling cannot decide the meaning.

steps.title: Blocking the reply that God really was not afflicted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shuts down a possible comeback: maybe the verse in ישעיהו really does mean God was not afflicted. No, because the same verse goes on to say His angel saved them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to say that it really does mean that (God was not afflicted), but look, it is written in the same verse, 'and the angel of His presence saved them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines someone saying the verse really does mean 'not afflicted', and rejects that by quoting the end of the same verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 brought a verse where ל־א seems to mean 'to Him'. Someone could argue it still means 'not'. The end of the verse shows God cared and saved them, so the meaning must be that God shared their pain.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (the גמרא anticipates a reply)
Indeed so, that is really the meaning
But is it not written?
The angel of His presence

phrases.english: And if you would say: indeed so,
but isn't it written: "And the angel of His presence saved them"!
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 63:9, the same verse quoted in the last step.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי, וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the pushback of step 6 by blocking a counter-reading of the ישעיהו verse.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the attempt to read ל־א in ישעיהו 63:9 as 'not'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rest of the verse, where God's angel saves them, shows that God did care, so reading it as 'not afflicted' does not fit.

steps.title: The spelling can mean either thing
steps.stepSummary: Conclusion: the spelling ל־א can sometimes mean 'not' and sometimes 'to Him', so the spelling in איוב does not settle the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not clear that it can mean this, and it can mean that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that ל־א does not always mean 'not', so we cannot decide איוב's case from spelling alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the question from step 5 (why was there any doubt?). Since the spelling can go both ways, the doubt in the משנה was real, and another proof is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that
It can mean this and it can mean that

steps.whatToRemember: The written spelling ל־א is not decisive: it can mean 'not' or 'to Him'. That is why the משנה needed another way to show איוב served from love.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that
it means this and it means that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, מַשְׁמַע הָכִי וּמַשְׁמַע הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from steps 6 and 7 and answers the question of step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because ל־א can mean either 'not' or 'to Him', the spelling alone cannot prove whether איוב served from love.

steps.title: רבי מאיר compares איוב to אברהם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי מאיר says both איוב and אברהם are called 'God-fearing'. Just as אברהם's fear was out of love, so was איוב's.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי מאיר says: 'God-fearing' is said about איוב, and 'God-fearing' is said about אברהם. Just as 'God-fearing' said about אברהם means out of love, so too 'God-fearing' said about איוב means out of love.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a different proof that איוב served God out of love, using a matching phrase in two places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the spelling did not settle it, רבי מאיר uses the same words, 'God-fearing', found about both people. Whatever is true of אברהם's 'fear' is applied to איוב's 'fear', so איוב also served from love.

keyTerms.meaning: God-fearing
Just as ... so too (comparing two cases)
Out of love

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the words are 'God-fearing', the point is that this 'fear' came from love, since that is what it means for אברהם.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir says:
"God-fearing" is said about Job,
phrases.notes: איוב 1:1

phrases.english: and "God-fearing" is said about Abraham.
phrases.notes: בראשית 22:12

phrases.english: Just as "God-fearing" said about Abraham means out of love,
so too "God-fearing" said about Job means out of love.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 8 showed the spelling is not decisive, this brings a different proof for the משנה's claim about איוב.
steps.raayaObject: That איוב served God out of love.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared phrase 'God-fearing' used for איוב (איוב 1:1) and for אברהם (בראשית 22:12).

steps.title: How do we know אברהם acted out of love?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that אברהם himself served from love, and answers with the verse 'the offspring of אברהם who loved Me'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אברהם himself, from where do we know (he served out of love)? As it is written: 'The offspring of אברהם, who loved Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר's proof depends on אברהם having served from love, so the גמרא asks for a source and gives a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison in step 9 only works if we already know אברהם's 'fear' was from love. The verse in ישעיהו calls אברהם 'who loved Me', which fills that gap.

keyTerms.meaning: Himself
From where do we know it?
As it is written
Who loved Me

phrases.english: And Abraham himself, from where do we know?
As it is written: "The offspring of Abraham who loved Me."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 41:8

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבְרָהָם גּוּפֵיהּ מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the assumption that step 9's comparison rests on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that אברהם served God out of love.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse 'זרע אברהם אהבי' (ישעיהו 41:8) calls אברהם one who loves God.

steps.title: What difference does love make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between someone who serves God out of love and someone who serves out of fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between one who acts out of love and one who acts out of fear?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why it matters whether איוב served from love or from fear. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both people are doing the מצוות. The question is whether the motive changes anything real.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is there between
One who does (the מצוות)
Out of fear

phrases.english: What difference is there between one who acts out of love
and one who acts out of fear?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין עוֹשֶׂה מֵאַהֲבָה לְעוֹשֶׂה מִיִּרְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving איוב served from love, the גמרא asks what that actually changes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between serving God from love and serving from fear.

steps.title: Love-based merit lasts two thousand generations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says serving from love is greater. Merit from fear lasts a thousand generations, and merit from love lasts two thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is what was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Greater is one who acts out of love than one who acts out of fear, because this one (fear) lasts for a thousand generations, and that one (love) lasts for two thousand generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: love-based service is greater, and its merit lasts twice as long.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is in the reward: how long the merit stays and protects the person's descendants. Fear-based merit stays for a thousand generations, and love-based merit stays for two thousand.

keyTerms.meaning: There is that which was taught
Greater ... than
Lasts, stays in place (his merit)
For two thousand generations

steps.whatToRemember: Serving God from love is greater than serving from fear. Its merit lasts two thousand generations compared to one thousand, and that is why it matters that איוב served from love.
steps.confusionAlert: The first 'this one' (זה) is the person who serves from fear (one thousand), and the second is the person who serves from love (two thousand).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the motive behind doing מצוות is not just a feeling. It changes how long the merit lasts.

phrases.english: There is that which was taught:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Greater is the one who acts out of love
than the one who acts out of fear,
for this one lasts for a thousand generations,
phrases.notes: 'This one' here is the person who serves out of fear; his merit stays a thousand generations.

phrases.english: and that one lasts for two thousand generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One who serves from love is greater: his merit lasts two thousand generations, while fear-based merit lasts one thousand.

steps.title: The proof from two פסוקים: thousands of generations versus one thousand
steps.stepSummary: The source for 'love lasts two thousand generations, fear lasts one thousand' is a comparison between a פסוק in עשרת הדברות ('thousands') and a פסוק in דברים ('a thousand').
steps.simpleTranslation: Here (in עשרת הדברות) it says: 'to thousands, to those who love Me and keep My commandments.' And there (in דברים) it says: 'and to those who keep His commandments, for a thousand generations.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוקים behind רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's statement in step 12. One פסוק says 'thousands' and the other says 'a thousand.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Thousands' in the plural means at least two thousand, and it appears next to 'those who love Me.' 'A thousand generations' is one thousand. So love earns at least two thousand generations of merit, and fear earns one thousand.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is written; this introduces the first פסוק of a comparison
And there it is written; this introduces the second פסוק to compare
To thousands (plural), meaning at least two thousand
For a thousand generations

phrases.english: Here it is written:
'to thousands, to those who love Me'
phrases.notes: 'Thousands' is plural, so the smallest it can mean is two thousand.

phrases.english: 'and to those who keep My commandments,'
phrases.notes: This is from עשרת הדברות in שמות פרק כ.

phrases.english: and there it is written:
'and to those who keep His commandments, for a thousand generations.'
phrases.notes: דברים 7:9

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא כְּתִיב וְהָתָם כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the numbers in רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That merit from love lasts two thousand generations and merit from fear lasts one thousand.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות פרק כ ('לאלפים לאהבי') compared with דברים 7:9 ('לאלף דור').

steps.title: The פסוק in דברים also mentions love
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: the פסוק in דברים that says 'a thousand generations' also says 'those who love Him.' So how can it be about fear?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there too it is written: 'to those who love Him and to those who keep His commandments, for a thousand generations'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from step 13. The 'thousand generations' פסוק also mentions people who love הקב״ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on 'a thousand' being for fear and 'thousands' being for love. But both פסוקים mention love together with keeping the מצוות. So it looks like love gets only one thousand in דברים, and the difference between the two פסוקים seems to disappear.

keyTerms.meaning: There too; points out that the other case has the same feature
To those who love Him

phrases.english: There too it is written
'to those who love Him and to those who keep His commandments'
phrases.notes: This is the full wording of the same פסוק in דברים 7:9. Step 13 quoted only its end.

phrases.english: 'for a thousand generations'!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק in דברים used in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'לאלף דור' refers only to those who serve from fear.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same פסוק mentions 'those who love Him,' so 'a thousand generations' seems to apply to love too.

steps.title: Each number goes with the phrase right next to it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in each פסוק the number belongs to the words right next to it. In דברים, 'a thousand generations' sits next to 'those who keep His commandments' (fear). In שמות, 'thousands' sits next to 'those who love Me' (love).
steps.simpleTranslation: This one refers to what is right next to it, and that one refers to what is right next to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by looking at word order. The number in each פסוק attaches to the phrase it is closest to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דברים, 'לאלף דור' comes right after 'ולשמרי מצותיו,' which does not mention love, so the thousand is about those who serve from fear. In שמות, 'לאלפים' comes right before 'לאהבי,' so 'thousands' is about those who serve from love. The proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To what is right next to it; a word goes with the phrase beside it
This one

steps.whatToRemember: Serving from love earns at least two thousand generations of merit, and serving from fear earns one thousand. We learn this from where 'thousands' and 'a thousand' sit in each פסוק.

phrases.english: This one refers to what is right next to it,
phrases.notes: In דברים, 'a thousand generations' is right after 'those who keep His commandments,' so it is about fear.

phrases.english: and that one refers to what is right next to it.
phrases.notes: In שמות, 'thousands' is right before 'those who love Me,' so it is about love.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי לְדִסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ וְהַאי לְדִסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 and keeps the proof of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading by closeness: each number is read with the phrase right next to it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים mention love, so 'a thousand generations' would apply to love as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'A thousand' goes with 'those who keep His commandments' (fear), and 'thousands' goes with 'those who love Me' (love).

steps.title: Two students tell רבא their dreams
steps.stepSummary: Two students sitting before רבא each tell him a פסוק they heard in a dream. One heard a פסוק about those who fear הקב״ה. The other heard a פסוק about those who love His name.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were two students sitting before רבא. One told him: 'They read to me in my dream: How great is Your goodness that You hid away for those who fear You.' The other told him: 'They read to me in my dream: All who trust in You will rejoice and sing forever, and those who love Your name will be joyful in You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to illustrate love versus fear. This step only describes the two dreams; it is setting up רבא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים match the two ways of serving. The first speaks of 'those who fear You' (יראה), and the second speaks of 'those who love Your name' (אהבה). The story connects to the topic just discussed.

keyTerms.meaning: Before רבא, in front of him as students
They read to me, they recited to me
In my dream
For those who fear You

phrases.english: There were these two students
who were sitting before רבא,
one said to him:
They read to me in my dream:
'How great is Your goodness'
'which You have hidden away for those who fear You,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 31:20

phrases.english: And the other said to him:
They read to me in my dream:
'And all who trust in You will rejoice,'
'they will sing forever,'
'and those who love Your name will be joyful in You.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 5:12

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ תְּרֵי תַּלְמִידֵי דַּהֲווֹ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the derivation from פסוקים to a story that illustrates love and fear.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two students heard different פסוקים in their dreams: one about fear and one about love.

steps.title: רבא explains: both are righteous, one from love and one from fear
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells the students that both of them are completely righteous. One serves from love and the other serves from fear, and each dream matched his way of serving.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Both of you, Sages, are completely righteous. One of you serves from love, and one of you serves from fear.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the two dreams. This finishes the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק in the dreams showed how that student serves הקב״ה. The one who heard 'those who love Your name' serves from love, and the one who heard 'those who fear You' serves from fear. Both are called צדיקים גמורים, so serving from fear is still full righteousness, even though step 12 said love is greater.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of you
Completely righteous people
Master; a polite way to refer to a scholar, here meaning 'one of you'

steps.whatToRemember: Serving from fear and serving from love are both complete righteousness. Love earns greater reward, but someone who serves from fear is still a צדיק גמור.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא says 'מר מאהבה' first, but that matches the second student, the one who dreamed of 'those who love Your name.' 'מר מיראה' matches the first student.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Both of you, Sages,
are completely righteous.
One Master serves from love,
phrases.notes: This is the second student, who dreamed about 'those who love Your name.'

phrases.english: and one Master serves from fear.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ תַּרְוַיְיכוּ רַבָּנַן צַדִּיקֵי גְּמוּרֵי אַתּוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's explanation of the dreams told in step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both kinds of service are complete righteousness: one student serves from love and one from fear, and each one's dream matched his way of serving.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing כשם שהמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally closes the chapter כשם שהמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter כשם שהמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter כשם שהמים is over, and the גמרא marks its end with the traditional הדרן line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new argument is being made here. It is a closing formula. It tells us the discussion about love and fear of הקב״ה, and the rest of this chapter, is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the closing words said when finishing a chapter
The name of the chapter now ending, taken from its opening words

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter "Just as the water"

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after רבא's ruling about the two students
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter כשם שהמים is complete.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: Any report of seclusion forces divorce
steps.stepSummary: A husband warned his wife and then heard, even from an unreliable source, that she secluded herself. He must divorce her and pay her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man warned his wife not to be alone with a certain man, and she was, even if he heard about it from a flying bird, he must divorce her and give her the כתובה. This is the view of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה. רבי אליעזר rules that after a קינוי (warning), even a flimsy report of her סתירה (seclusion) means the husband must divorce her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the wife goes through the bitter-water process. Here no proper witnesses saw the seclusion, so she cannot drink. רבי אליעזר still says the husband must send her away. She keeps her כתובה because nothing was actually proven against her.

keyTerms.meaning: He warned his wife not to be alone with a specific man (קינוי)
She secluded herself with that man (סתירה)
A flying bird, meaning any source at all, even an unreliable one
He must divorce her
The marriage contract money owed to the wife

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the husband must divorce her, she still gets her כתובה. The report is enough to end the marriage. It is not enough to punish her financially.

phrases.english: One who warned his wife, and she secluded herself,
even if he heard it from a flying bird,
phrases.notes: This is a way of saying "from any source at all," even one that would not count as real testimony.

phrases.english: he must divorce her and give her the marriage contract money,
these are the words of רבי אליעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁקִּינֵּא לְאִשְׁתּוֹ וְנִסְתְּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter מי שקינא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a warning, even an unreliable report of seclusion obligates divorce, with payment of the כתובה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: Only when the town gossip spreads
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the husband does not have to divorce her until the women spinning by moonlight are talking about her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: not until the women who spin thread by moonlight discuss her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע disagrees with רבי אליעזר. He needs much more than a passing rumor before the husband must divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rumor from "a bird" is not enough for רבי יהושע. The talk must be widespread, the kind of gossip that even the women spinning at night are passing around. So the argument is about how strong the report must be.

keyTerms.meaning: They discuss her, they talk about her
Women who spin thread
The moon

phrases.english: רבי יהושע says:
not until they discuss her,
phrases.notes: The words "he does not divorce her" are left out but assumed. רבי יהושע is answering רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: the women who spin by the light of the moon.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיִּשְׂאוּ וְיִתְּנוּ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אליעזר's ruling in the previous step
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divorce is only required once there is widespread public gossip about her.

steps.title: One witness to defilement stops her from drinking
steps.stepSummary: If one witness says he saw her become defiled, she does not drink the bitter water.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one witness said, "I saw that she became defiled," she would not drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new case. One witness says the wife actually sinned, and so she does not go through the bitter-water test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one witness is not enough in court. Here, though, a single עד אחד who saw her defiled is believed. The water test only checks a doubt, and his testimony removes the doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A single witness
She became defiled, meaning she committed adultery
Drinks, referring to the bitter water of a סוטה

phrases.english: If one witness said,
"I saw that she became defiled,"
she would not drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עֵד אֶחָד אֲנִי רְאִיתִיהָ שֶׁנִּטְמֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from reports about seclusion to testimony about the act of defilement itself
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single witness to defilement is believed, and she does not drink.

steps.title: Even a slave or maidservant is believed, and she loses her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: Even an עבד or a שפחה is believed as that one witness, strongly enough to take away her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more than that: even a slave or a maidservant is believed, even to make her lose her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes a step further than the last case. Even people who usually cannot testify are believed here, and their testimony costs her the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד and a שפחה are normally not valid witnesses. Here their word is accepted. It does more than stop her from drinking: it also takes away her כתובה money. This is the strongest result in the משנה so far.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but even more
A slave, normally not a valid witness
A maidservant
They are believed
To disqualify her, meaning she loses her rights

steps.whatToRemember: The ladder of this משנה: רבי אליעזר says any report of seclusion forces divorce, but she keeps her כתובה. רבי יהושע needs widespread gossip. One witness to defilement stops her from drinking. Even a slave or maidservant is believed, and she loses her כתובה too.

phrases.english: And not only that, but
even a slave, even a maidservant,
these are believed,
even to disqualify her from her marriage contract money.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ עֶבֶד אֲפִילּוּ שִׁפְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the single-witness rule to normally invalid witnesses and adds loss of the כתובה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a slave or maidservant is believed about her defilement, and she loses her כתובה.

steps.title: Certain female relatives are believed only to stop her from drinking
steps.stepSummary: Her mother-in-law, mother-in-law's daughter, co-wife, sister-in-law, and husband's daughter are believed that she was defiled. Their word only stops her from drinking. It does not take away her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her mother-in-law, her mother-in-law's daughter, her co-wife, her sister-in-law, and her husband's daughter are believed. But they are not believed to make her lose her כתובה. They are only believed so that she does not drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a list of women who may testify that she was defiled. Their testimony has a limited effect: she does not drink, but she keeps her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22, even an עבד or a שפחה was believed strongly enough to take away her כתובה. These relatives get a weaker result. Their testimony stops the drinking, but it does not cost her the כתובה money.

keyTerms.meaning: Her mother-in-law (the husband's mother)
Her co-wife (another wife of the same husband)
Her sister-in-law (the wife of her husband's brother)
They are believed
To make her lose her כתובה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 22. There, an עבד or a שפחה could take away her כתובה. Here, these relatives can only stop the drinking.

phrases.english: Her mother-in-law and her mother-in-law's daughter
and her co-wife, and her sister-in-law, and her husband's daughter
phrases.notes: Here יבמתה means her husband's brother's wife, and the husband's daughter is his daughter from another wife.

phrases.english: these are believed.
But not to disqualify her from her כתובה,
but only so that she does not drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ נֶאֱמָנוֹת וְלֹא לְפוֹסְלָהּ מִכְּתוּבָּתָהּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁתֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second group of witnesses whose testimony has a weaker effect than the עבד or the שפחה in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These female relatives are believed about defilement only to stop her from drinking. She does not lose her כתובה.

steps.title: Logic would have required two witnesses for defilement
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents a קל וחומר. Testimony about seclusion, which only forbids her for a while, needs two witnesses. So testimony about defilement, which forbids her forever, should also need two.
steps.simpleTranslation: It would have made sense to say this: the first testimony (about seclusion) does not forbid her forever, and still it needs two witnesses. The final testimony (about defilement) forbids her forever. Surely it should also need two witnesses!
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains why the rule of one witness has to be taught at all. It shows that simple logic would have pointed the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony about seclusion can be undone, since she may drink and be found innocent. Testimony about defilement forbids her to her husband forever. Since the lighter testimony needs two witnesses, the heavier one should need at least two as well.

keyTerms.meaning: For it would have been logical
An argument from a lighter case to a heavier case
The first testimony: that she secluded herself
The final testimony: that she was defiled
A permanent prohibition

phrases.english: For it would have been logical:
Just as the first testimony,
phrases.notes: The first testimony is the one about seclusion; the final one is about defilement.

phrases.english: which does not forbid her forever,
is not established with fewer than two,
then the final testimony,
which forbids her forever,
is it not logical
that it should not be established with fewer than two?

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהָיָה בַּדִּין וּמָה אִם עֵדוּת רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the rule that one witness is enough (steps 21 to 23) needs a source, by showing that logic points the other way.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 21 that one witness about defilement is enough to stop her from drinking.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seclusion testimony is lighter and needs two witnesses. Defilement testimony is heavier, so by קל וחומר it should need two as well.

steps.title: The verse teaches that even one witness is enough
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ' shows that she drinks only when there is no witness at all. Any testimony against her, even one witness, stops the drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And there is no witness against her.' This means any testimony at all that there is against her counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the קל וחומר from step 24 with a פסוק. The verse overrides the logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She drinks only when there is 'no witness' at all. So if there is any witness, even just one, she does not drink. That is why the קל וחומר does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches
'And there is no witness against her' (במדבר 5:13)

steps.whatToRemember: One witness about defilement is enough to stop her from drinking. This comes from the verse 'וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ', even though a קל וחומר would have required two.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states:
"And there is no witness against her,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:13

phrases.english: meaning any testimony that there is against her.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 24 with a verse.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A verse overrides the logical argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Defilement testimony should need two witnesses, like seclusion testimony.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse 'וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ' teaches that any testimony, even one witness, is enough to stop her from drinking.

steps.title: Setting up a new קל וחומר about the seclusion testimony
steps.stepSummary: Now that one witness is enough for defilement, the משנה begins a new קל וחומר. It suggests that one witness should also be enough for the seclusion testimony. The argument continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that this is settled, there is a קל וחומר for the first testimony: just as if...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up its next move. It turns the conclusion of step 25 into an argument about the seclusion testimony, and the sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 showed that the heavier testimony (defilement) needs only one witness. So the lighter testimony (seclusion) should need only one as well. This reverses the direction of the קל וחומר from step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: From now (now that this is established)

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished on this amud. The full argument and its answer come on the next amud.

phrases.english: And from now, a קל וחומר can be made for the first testimony:
Just as if...

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַל וָחוֹמֶר לְעֵדוּת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the conclusion of step 25 and begins using it against the rule that seclusion needs two witnesses.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the seclusion testimony needs two witnesses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the heavier defilement testimony needs only one witness, the lighter seclusion testimony should also need only one (completed on the next amud).
